approach: Change the loop in plan_round (planning.rs). Each critic round runs an inner loop of planning_round calls. When Athena's plan rules (plan_findings) give a Blocker or Major finding, planning_round returns a new RoundEnd::Mechanical(PlanRevision) instead of calling end_round. That variant is not filed as a record, calls no critic and does not advance the critic round. The loop re-invokes the planner with the finding in the revision brief. After MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES (2) such passes in one critic round, a plan that still breaks a rule is filed with its Athena-only critique and the job stops in planning with that finding. Plan and critique records stay keyed by critic round, so the critic sees "round 1" on the first plan it reviews and max_rounds counts only critic reviews. New tests go in mod.rs and use the fake driver. Five existing CLI tests that read an Athena-only critique-1 are adjusted to the new numbering (test-only edit outside the listed deliverables, forced by the new numbering). CHANGELOG.md and job-planning.md are updated.

decisions.choice: Mechanical plans are not filed as job-plan-N and critique-N records. The plan and critique of a round are filed only when the critic reviews the plan, or at the final mechanical stop.
decisions.reason: Records are keyed by round, and the critic brief and revision brief print plan.round. Criterion 1 needs the critic to see the fixed plan as round 1. Each mechanical attempt keeps its planner invocation record, and its findings reach the planner in the revision brief. Nothing validates that rounds are contiguous: store.rs only sorts them, and the resume seed takes the max round and that round's critique.

rejected.option: File every planner output under an increasing record number, so mechanical attempts take critique-1 and critique-2 with no critic.
rejected.why: The critic would be shown 'round 3' for its first review, which contradicts criterion 1, and the numbers would be read as planning rounds in status, reasons and briefs.

rejected.option: Add an attempt field to the JobPlan and Critique records.
rejected.why: It needs a record schema change and a records allow-list change, which the brief rules out, and it is larger than this fix needs.

rejected.option: Keep the old record numbering so the CLI tests need no edit.
rejected.why: Those tests assert that critique-1 is Athena-only with no critic invocation. That cannot hold while the critic's first review is round 1 (criterion 1), so the edit to those tests is unavoidable.

decisions.choice: The cap of two mechanical passes applies per critic round, as the accepted reading says. It is the constant MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES = 2 in planning.rs, counted in plan_round's loop and enforced in planning_round.
decisions.reason: It matches the accepted reading and keeps the rule simple. The extra planner cost per round is bounded, and every planner call still goes through check_budget.

rejected.option: A job-wide cap of two mechanical passes.
rejected.why: A later round's revision could then be stopped by a mechanical finding with no pass left, which recreates the problem.
A planner that cannot satisfy a rule would loop and spend money. The request asks for at most two passes.

decisions.choice: planning_round takes a small Attempt struct { round, mechanical_passes, resumed_from } in place of the bare round argument.
decisions.reason: It keeps the argument count within clippy's limit, and it carries a seeded resume's resumed_from across mechanical passes, because the Mechanical PlanRevision does not carry it and the brief heading depends on it.

decisions.choice: The final mechanical stop files the plan and an Athena-only Revise critique at the current round, then calls stop_planning with a reason 'the plan still broke Athena's own plan rules after 2 mechanical revisions (round r of M). Findings: ...' built with findings_line. It does not use PLANNING_CAP_REASON.
decisions.reason: The stop keeps the finding as evidence. planning_resume_seed matches only PLANNING_CAP_REASON, so a mechanical stop is not offered as a resume seed; its plan was never critic-reviewed. Round r has no critic record yet, so there is no filename collision.

rejected.option: Reuse end_round with last_round set to true.
rejected.why: It would report the cap reason, and the resume logic would treat the stop as a critic-reviewed cap.

files.purpose: Add MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES, the Attempt struct and RoundEnd::Mechanical. Give plan_round an inner pass loop. In planning_round, the plan_findings branch returns Mechanical, or files the plan and critique and stops after the cap. Update the plan_round doc comment and the UI line.
Tests only: repo_with_config/repo_with_planning, a logging scripted planner and critic wrapper over base_script, bad and good plan helpers, and the three new tests.
Unreleased entry for the new round accounting and the two-pass cap.
Update 'Athena's own checks', 'Rounds and cost' and the 'Built as' note for build job 4: a major finding goes back without a model call and without using a round, up to two passes per round.

Not a listed deliverable; test-only and forced. Five tests (governance file, command outside the grant, fails_without/criterion count, file existence, directory) read an Athena-only critique-1, which becomes the critic's under the new numbering. Change only those assertions, to check the planner's second brief and the critic call count.

steps: In planning.rs, add `pub(super) const MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES: u32 = 2;` with a doc comment. Add `struct Attempt { round: u32, mechanical_passes: u32, resumed_from: Option<JobId> }` and the `RoundEnd::Mechanical(Box<PlanRevision>)` variant.

Rewrite plan_round. Take resumed_from from the seed. For each critic round 1..=max_rounds, run `loop { planning_round(..., Attempt, revision.take()) }`. Handle Accepted and Stopped as now. On Revise, set the revision and break to the next critic round. On Mechanical, increment the pass count, set the revision and continue the loop. Pass resumed_from only while round == 1. Update the doc comment: only critic reviews count toward max_rounds, and Athena's rule findings get up to MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES immediate revisions per round with no critic call.

In planning_round, switch the signature to Attempt. In the plan_findings Blocker/Major branch, build the Athena-only critique as today. If mechanical_passes < MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES, print 'athena     plan round {round}: {n} finding(s); no critic call; revising (pass k of 2)' and return Mechanical with PlanRevision { previous: plan, findings, resumed_from: None }, without filing records. Otherwise push the plan and critique to closing, call stop_planning with the new reason built by findings_line, and return Stopped.

In mod.rs tests, turn repo() into a wrapper over repo_with_config(extra: &str) that appends extra to the stripped athena.toml. Add repo_with_planning(max_rounds), a bad plan JSON (README.md create) and a good plan JSON (README.md modify, one demonstration for criterion 1), and a planning_script wrapper over base_script that logs roles and prompts and serves planner and critic turns from queues. Add the three tests.

Run `cargo test --locked`. In crates/athena-cli/tests/job_plan.rs change only the five tests that read an Athena-only critique-1: assert that the planner's second brief contains the finding and that critique-1 is now the critic's. Keep the planner and critic call counts.
Add the CHANGELOG.md entry under [Unreleased]. Update docs/design/job-planning.md in the places listed in files.
Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`.

risks.risk: The CLI tests in job_plan.rs, and possibly others, read an Athena-only critique-1 and break with the new numbering.
risks.mitigation: Step 5 adjusts them. The producer runs cargo test --locked and fixes each failure by asserting on the planner's revision brief and the critic call count, test-only.

risks.risk: A mechanical pass reuses the plan-{round} snapshot directory and the planner's seq numbers.
risks.mitigation: planning_round already removes the snapshot tree before creating it and after use, and ctx.next_seq(closing) is monotonic per invocation, so invocation records do not collide.

risks.risk: A seeded resume's resumed_from is lost on a mechanical pass, so the final plan record loses its resumed_from field.
risks.mitigation: Attempt carries resumed_from for every pass of the seeded round (round 1 only).

risks.risk: Extra planner calls raise the cost of a hard job.
risks.mitigation: At most two passes per round, check_budget before every planner call, and a budget stop ends planning as before.

risks.risk: The final mechanical stop files a plan and critique at the current round number, which could collide with a critic record.
risks.mitigation: The current round has no critic record yet when the stop occurs. The stop path pushes exactly one plan and one critique, and test 3 plus athena.check_history in the CLI tests cover it.

demonstrations.method: New test in the produce_and_verify_order_tests module of crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs. It drives Athena::go, the production entry point, over a repo built by repo_with_planning(max_rounds = 3). The seam is the fake agent driver (FakeAgentDriver::new(script)), which exists today and is injected through athena_with. The script wraps base_script. It logs each role and user_prompt. The planner returns a bad plan first (README.md with action create although it exists, which breaks the real plan rule 'creates a file that exists') and a good plan after. The critic returns accept. Step 4 adds repo_with_planning, the planner and critic turns and the logging wrapper, all in the test module. The test does not stub plan_findings or the brief. Guards: [job_plan] enabled with mode all, and a capability that does not pin the repo (base_script's reader returns 'study').
demonstrations.observes: The role log is [Reader, Planner, Planner, Critic, Producer, Verifier]. The second planner prompt contains 'already exists in the base'. The first critic prompt contains '## Plan under review (round 1)'. The job state is Landed.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the new loop, the first plan's finding ends round 1 with no critic call. The critic's first prompt would say 'Plan under review (round 2)', so the round-1 assertion and the Reader, Planner, Planner, Critic order assertion fail.

demonstrations.method: New test in the same module, with the same entry point, seam and wrapper, using repo_with_planning(max_rounds = 3). The planner returns one bad plan, then good plans. The critic returns revise with a major finding every time.
demonstrations.observes: The role log is [Reader, Planner, Planner, Critic, Planner, Critic, Planner, Critic] with no Producer. The critic prompts name rounds 1, 2 and 3 in order. The job is Failed, and the reason starts with PLANNING_STOPPED_PREFIX and contains PLANNING_CAP_REASON and 'round 3 of 3'.
demonstrations.fails_without: Under the old accounting the mechanical finding takes round 1, only two critic calls occur before the cap stop, and the reason says 'round 2 of 3'. The three-critic-call assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: New test in the same module, with the same entry point, seam and wrapper, using repo_with_planning(max_rounds = 5). The planner always returns the bad plan. The critic arm of the script panics, so any critic call fails the test.
demonstrations.observes: The planner is called exactly three times (first plan plus two mechanical passes) and the critic never. The job is Failed. The reason starts with PLANNING_STOPPED_PREFIX and contains 'already exists in the base' and 'after 2 mechanical revisions', and does not contain PLANNING_CAP_REASON. No Producer or Verifier ran.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the pass cap the planner is called again each time and planning never stops on the mechanical finding. Under the old accounting max_rounds = 5 gives five planner calls and a cap-style reason. The exact planner-call count, the zero critic calls and the reason assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff of planning.rs. Four things must be present: (1) the plan_findings branch no longer calls end_round with last_round; (2) a pub(super) const MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES: u32 = 2 with a doc comment; (3) plan_round's doc comment says only critic reviews count toward max_rounds and describes the mechanical passes; (4) RoundEnd::Mechanical exists and plan_round's loop handles it without advancing the round. Criteria 1 to 3 show the behavior; this checks content.
demonstrations.observes: The four items above are present in the diff.

The [Unreleased] section has an entry saying findings from Athena's own plan rules go back to the planner without using a planning round or calling the critic, at most two passes per round, and that only critic reviews count toward max_rounds. It names the 2026-10-28 cause: a missing fails_without and a grouped command line took rounds 1 and 2.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks Athena runs on the result, in order, from the repository root. The test run includes the three new tests and the adjusted CLI job_plan tests; clippy covers the new Attempt struct and RoundEnd::Mechanical variant (unused fields or too many arguments would fail it); fmt covers formatting.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.fails_without: If the loop change were made without adjusting the five CLI tests in job_plan.rs, cargo test --locked would fail on them, because critique-1 would be the critic's and not Athena-only. If the Attempt struct left an unused field or planning_round kept too many arguments, clippy -D warnings would fail. If the new code were unformatted, fmt --check would fail.

demonstrations.method: Run the existing planning tests: the critic-soundness tests in mod.rs, the revise, reject and last-round cases, the resume-seed tests, and the CLI job_plan and lifecycle tests. Only the five CLI tests that read an Athena-only critique-1 are adjusted, and they assert on the planner's revision brief and the critic call count instead, which covers the same behavior.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core && cargo test -p athena-cli --test job_plan --test lifecycle
demonstrations.observes: All pass. Critic-reviewed paths keep their record numbering (job-plan-N and critique-N for N = 1 to 3), the cap reason and the resume seed.
demonstrations.fails_without: A regression in end_round, in the resume seed or in max_rounds accounting would break these tests, including the critic-soundness tests in mod.rs, the 'revise in the last round' case and a_retry_of_a_job_stopped_in_planning_carries_the_last_critiques_findings.

open_questions: Should the cap be job-wide instead of per critic round? The plan follows the accepted reading (per round). The worst case adds 6 planner calls (3 rounds x 2), each checked by check_budget.
Mechanical attempts are no longer in the records except through their planner invocation records. Keeping the mechanical findings in a record would need a schema change, which is out of scope.
